newsitem.title: USA: Amoco, Shell Permian Basin talks stalled.
newsitem.headline: Amoco, Shell Permian Basin talks stalled.

text.p: Talks between Amoco Corp and Shell Oil Co on forming a joint venture to merge the two companies' oil and gas operations in the Permian Basin have stalled, the Houston Chronicle reported on Wednesday.
Talks snagged on a "significant issue" that was the focus of a November 18 meeting in Chicago between senior executives from the two companies working out details of the venture, the newspaper said.
"The result of the meeting was that negotiations are at an impasse," Jim Posey, vice president of Amoco's Permian Basin operations, said in a memo obtained by the newspaper.

Posey was slated to run the joint venture company, to be named Altura Energy, which would have merged the two companies' oil and gas operations in west Texas and eastern New Mexico to form the third-largest U.S. independent oil and gas producer.

A Shell spokeswoman declined to discuss the agenda of the Chicago meeting, but told the Chronicle the venture had not been scrapped. "If all the issues are resolved, Amoco and Shell still intend to close the deal," she said.
Shell Oil is a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
